title: 08 — Design a URL Shortener
html:
08 — Design a URL Shortener

The one idea: generate a unique numeric ID (→ chapter 07), encode it in base62, store short → long in a key-value lookup, and serve redirects from cache. It's a read-heavy system where the short-code scheme is the only genuinely interesting decision.

Step 1 — Scope

  • Shorten: long URL → short URL like https://sho.rt/zn9edcu.
  • Redirect: short URL → long URL.
  • 100M URLs created per day; short URL as short as possible; characters [0-9a-zA-Z]; URLs can't be updated or deleted (simplification).
  • High availability, scalability, fault tolerance.

Estimates

  • Writes: 100M ÷ 10^5 ≈ 1,160/s
  • Reads at 10:1 → ~11,600/s
  • 10 years: 100M × 365 × 10 ≈ 365 billion records
  • Avg URL 100 B → ~36.5 TB

Code length: 62n ≥ 365 × 109 → n = 7 (62^7 ≈ 3.5 trillion).

Step 2 — High-level design

API

POST /api/v1/data/shorten      { "longUrl": "..." }   → 201 { "shortUrl": "..." }
GET  /{shortCode}                                      → 301/302 Location: longUrl

301 vs 302

Code Browser behaviour Use when
301 Moved Permanently Caches the redirect; later clicks skip your server Reducing server load matters most
302 Found Every click hits your server You need click analytics

Data model

url(id bigint PK, short_code char(7) unique, long_url varchar, created_at) — plus a unique index on long_url (or its hash) if duplicates should reuse the same code.

---
title: URL shortener — high-level architecture
---
flowchart LR
    U["User"] --> LB["Load balancer"]
    LB --> W["Web servers"]
    W -->|"GET code"| C[("Cache<br/>code → longUrl")]
    C -->|miss| DB[("DB")]
    W -->|"POST shorten"| IDG["ID generator"]
    IDG --> W
    W --> DB

Step 3 — Deep dive

3.1 Hash function options

A. Hash + collision resolution

  • Take CRC32/MD5/SHA-1 of the long URL, keep the first 7 characters.
  • On collision, append a salt and rehash; repeat.
  • Needs a DB lookup per attempt → use a Bloom filter to check existence cheaply.

B. Base62 conversion of a unique ID ✅

  • Get a unique ID (Snowflake or a DB sequence), convert to base62.
Hash + collision Base62 of ID
Length Fixed Grows with the ID (short early on)
Needs ID generator No Yes
Collisions Possible → retries Impossible
Predictable next code No Yes (a security consideration — see below) 
static string ToBase62(long value)
{
    const string alphabet = "0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ";
    if (value == 0) return "0";
    Span<char> buffer = stackalloc char[11];
    int i = buffer.Length;
    while (value > 0) { buffer[--i] = alphabet[(int)(value % 62)]; value /= 62; }
    return new string(buffer[i..]);
}

3.2 Shorten flow

  1. Is longUrl already in the DB? → return the existing code.
  2. Else generate ID → base62 → store (id, code, longUrl) → return.

3.3 Redirect flow

  1. Look up code in cache (Redis) → hit → redirect.
  2. Miss → DB → populate cache → redirect.
  3. Unknown code → 404.

With ~11.6k reads/s and a strong 80/20 popularity skew, the cache absorbs most traffic.

Step 4 — Wrap-up

  • Rate limiting on POST /shorten per user/IP (→ chapter 04) — shorteners attract spam.
  • Predictable IDs: base62 of sequential IDs lets people enumerate URLs. Mitigate with an obfuscating bijection (e.g. multiply by a large prime mod 62^7, or a Feistel cipher) before encoding.
  • Malicious URLs: check against a phishing/malware list on creation and on redirect.
  • Analytics: with 302, emit a click event to a queue → stream aggregation (→ chapter 21).
  • Scaling: web tier is stateless; DB is sharded by id or short_code; replicas for reads.
  • Custom aliases & expiry: unique index on alias; TTL column + background cleanup.

.NET / Azure mapping

  • Redirect endpoint as a minimal API: app.MapGet("/{code}", async (string code, IUrlStore store) => ... Results.Redirect(url, permanent: false)).
  • Output caching (AddOutputCache) or Redis via IDistributedCache for hot codes; HybridCache (.NET 9) gives L1 in-memory + L2 Redis with stampede protection.
  • Storage: Cosmos DB with shortCode as both id and partition key → single-digit-ms point reads at any scale; or Azure SQL with a SEQUENCE for IDs.
  • Front Door caches 301 responses at the edge.

Review checklist

  • Estimate → 7-character code justified with 62^7.
  • 301 vs 302 trade-off.
  • Hash+collision vs base62(ID) compared; one chosen.
  • Cache on the redirect path.
  • Rate limiting, enumeration and abuse addressed.
